data.gender_notes: Shristi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The power to create or bring about a new beginning, an idea or a work of art. A manifestation of the divine power of creation. The name Shristi carries the meaning “Creation” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Shristi usually hope their child will grow to embody creation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine power of creation and the potential within each individual to create their own destiny.
data.etymology: Shristi belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Creation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shristi total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_sanskrit.name: श्रिष्टि
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The goddess of creation, prosperity, and welfare. The root word is श्रि (shri) meaning wealth, prosperity, and good fortune.

in_hindi.name: श्रिष्टि
in_hindi.long_meaning: श्रेष्ठ (shreshth) meaning excellent or superior and शुभकारी (shubhkari) meaning auspicious or propitious. Together, it means 'Goddess of Prosperity, Wealth, and Auspiciousness'.

in_tamil.name: ஶ்ரீஷ்ரீதி
in_tamil.meaning: வரும்பு, மக்கள்களுக்கு வாழ்த்தல், வலியல், சிவக்கு, கோபம்
in_tamil.long_meaning: வரும்பு (varumbu) meaning prosperity, மக்கள்களுக்கு (makkalukkku) meaning for the welfare of people, வலியல் (valil) meaning wealth, சிவக்கு (civakku) meaning auspicious, and கோபம் (kopam) meaning desire or wish. Together, it means 'Goddess of Prosperity, Wealth, Desire, and Auspiciousness'.

in_telugu.name: శ్రీష్రీధి
in_telugu.long_meaning: The goddess of prosperity, wealth, and welfare. The root word is శ్రీ (shri) meaning wealth, prosperity, and good fortune.

It is a meaningful name for a child as it instills in them a sense of responsibility and power to bring about positive changes in the world. The name is also commonly used in Hindu art and literature to refer to the divine power of creation.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name "Shristi" is considered to be a divine power, a manifestation of Brahma, the creator god. The name reflects the belief that all creation comes from the divine and that individuals have the power to bring about a new beginning, not just in the physical world but also in their own spiritual growth. The name is a reminder that each of us has the power to create our own lives, our own destinies, and our own karma. It is an inspiring name that encourages individuals to strive for spiritual growth and to use their creative abilities to make a positive impact on the world.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shristi signifies the creative power or the divine artisan within us. It is the primal energy that brought the universe into existence and continues to shape our experiences.

historical_references.time_period: Originated with the earliest Hindu texts, likely around 1500 BCE
historical_references.context: Ancient Hindu texts like the Rigveda and the Upanishads mention the concept of Shristi as the divine power that created the universe. It is often associated with the supreme deity Brahman, who is the source of all creation.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Shristi can be found in the Puranic literature, specifically in the Bhagavata Purana. In this text, Shristi is personified as the goddess Devi, who creates the universe through her divine power.

This personification of Shristi reflects the later development of Hinduism, which placed greater emphasis on the worship of gods and goddesses.

It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
